scenarios.name: debug-failing-job-offline-config
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it creates a project .actrc with the -P mapping and --container-architecture linux/amd64, runs `act -j test` with --secret-file and -v, and explicitly checks that Docker is running; A puts the config in ~/.actrc rather than a project file and only says to start Docker in a comment, though its mapping, flags and run command are otherwise correct.

scenarios.name: skip-slack-step-and-pass-dispatch-inputs
scenarios.rationale: B covers every rubric element (--var-file, --secret-file, the ACT guard, throwaway values, .gitignore), while A gives the right command and ACT guard but never mentions .gitignore and leans on inline values over files.

scenarios.name: job-level-skip-and-dry-run-validation
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric directly: it explains that job-level `if:` can't see `env`, uses an event file `{"act": true}` with `!github.event.act`, and gives `act --validate`, `-n` and `-g`. B leads with an actor-based check, only mentions the event file as a fallback, and omits `--validate`, so it covers less of the rubric.
